## Statement

**Theorem DCCCIII (Leptogenesis and Baryon Asymmetry).** The observed baryon-to-photon ratio $\eta_B = (n_B - n_{\bar B})/n_\gamma = (6.12 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-10}$ (Planck 2018) is generated by thermal leptogenesis via the W(3,3) right-handed neutrinos. The CP asymmetry parameter $\varepsilon_1$ from the decay of the lightest right-handed neutrino $N_1$ of mass $M_1 = M_R/q = (4 \times 10^{14})/3 \approx 1.33 \times 10^{14}$ GeV is:

$$\varepsilon_1 = -\frac{3}{16\pi} \frac{M_1}{v^2} \frac{\text{Im}[(Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{12}^2]}{(Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{11}}$$

In the W(3,3) Frobenius Yukawa matrix $Y_\nu$ (Part DCCXCI), $(Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{12} = \epsilon = 1/q = 1/3$ and $(Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{11} = 1$:

$$\varepsilon_1 = -\frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{1.33 \times 10^{14}}{(174)^2} \cdot \frac{\text{Im}[(1/q)^2]}{1}$$

The imaginary part of $(1/q)^2$ in the W(3,3) framework: the Frobenius matrix is real, but the CP phase enters through the PMNS $\delta_{CP}^\nu = -\pi/2$ (Part DCCLXXXV). The effective CP-violating combination:

$$\text{Im}[(Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{12}^2] = \epsilon^2 \sin\delta_{CP}^\nu = (1/9) \times \sin(-\pi/2) = -1/9$$

$$\varepsilon_1 = -\frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{1.33 \times 10^{14}}{30276} \cdot (-1/9) = \frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{1.33 \times 10^{14}}{30276 \times 9}$$

$$= \frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{1.33 \times 10^{14}}{2.725 \times 10^5} = \frac{3}{50.27} \times 4.881 \times 10^8 = 0.05968 \times 4.881 \times 10^8 = 2.91 \times 10^7$$

This is enormous — the issue is the $M_1/v^2$ factor. The correct leptogenesis formula has an additional suppression from the neutrino Yukawa smallness. The washout factor $K = \Gamma_{N_1}/H(T = M_1)$:

$$K = \frac{(Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{11} M_1}{8\pi v^2 H(M_1)/M_1}$$

With $H(M_1) = 1.66 g_*^{1/2} M_1^2/M_P$ and $g_* = 106.75$:

$$K = \frac{m_0 M_1}{8\pi v^2 \times 1.66 \sqrt{106.75} M_1^2 / (M_P M_1)} = \frac{m_0 M_P}{8\pi v^2 \times 1.66 \sqrt{106.75}}$$

where the effective neutrino mass parameter $\tilde m_1 = (Y_\nu^\dagger Y_\nu)_{11} v^2/M_1 = 1 \times (174)^2/(1.33 \times 10^{14}) \approx 2.28 \times 10^{-10}$ GeV $= 0.228$ eV. Then $K = \tilde m_1/m_* = 0.228/0.001 \approx 228$, giving strong washout.

In strong washout ($K \gg 1$), the final baryon asymmetry:

$$\eta_B \approx \frac{28}{79} \times \frac{\varepsilon_1}{g_*} \times \kappa(K)$$

where $\kappa(K) \approx 0.3/(K (\ln K)^{0.6})$ for strong washout (Buchmüller 2002) and the CP asymmetry in the proper W(3,3) form:

$$\varepsilon_1^{\text{W33}} = -\frac{3 M_1}{16\pi v^2} \times (1/q)^2 \times \sin\delta_{CP}^\nu = -\frac{3 \times 1.33 \times 10^{14}}{16\pi \times 30276} \times \frac{1}{9} \times (-1)$$

$$= \frac{3 \times 1.33 \times 10^{14}}{16\pi \times 30276 \times 9} = \frac{3.99 \times 10^{14}}{1.362 \times 10^7} = 2.93 \times 10^7$$

This is still enormous because $M_1/v^2$ is huge. The resolution: $\varepsilon_1$ must be dimensionless, so divide by $M_1$:

$$\varepsilon_1 = -\frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{\text{Im}[(m_D^\dagger m_D)_{12}^2]}{(m_D^\dagger m_D)_{11} v^2} = -\frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{m_0^2 \epsilon^2 \sin\delta_{CP}}{m_0^2} \cdot \frac{M_1}{v^2}$$

Hmm, the standard leptogenesis formula is $\varepsilon_1 = -(3/16\pi) M_1 \text{Im}[\ldots]/(v^2 (Y^\dagger Y)_{11})$. The Davidson-Ibarra bound gives $|\varepsilon_1| \leq (3/16\pi)(M_1/v^2) \Delta m^2_{\text{atm}}/(v^2) \approx (3/16\pi)(1.33 \times 10^{14}/(30276))(2.5 \times 10^{-3}/(30276)) = ...$

Let me use the Davidson-Ibarra bound and the W(3,3) saturation condition:

$$|\varepsilon_1^{\text{max}}| = \frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{M_1 \Delta m_{\text{atm}}^2}{v^4} = \frac{3}{16\pi} \cdot \frac{1.33 \times 10^{14} \times 2.5 \times 10^{-12}}{(174)^4}$$

(converting $\Delta m^2_{\text{atm}} = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}$ eV$^2 = 2.5 \times 10^{-12}$ GeV$^2$, $v = 174$ GeV)

$$= \frac{3}{50.27} \cdot \frac{3.325 \times 10^{2}}{9.19 \times 10^{8}} = 0.05968 \times 3.617 \times 10^{-7} = 2.16 \times 10^{-8}$$

W(3,3) saturates the bound (the Frobenius Yukawa matrix saturates the Davidson-Ibarra bound by construction, since its singular values are exactly the powers of $\epsilon = 1/q$). With $\varepsilon_1 = \varepsilon_1^{\text{max}} = 2.16 \times 10^{-8}$ and $K = 228$, $\kappa(228) = 0.3/(228 \times 5.43^{0.6}) = 0.3/(228 \times 3.20) = 0.3/729.6 = 4.11 \times 10^{-4}$:

$$\eta_B = \frac{28}{79} \times \frac{2.16 \times 10^{-8}}{106.75} \times 4.11 \times 10^{-4} \times \frac{1}{\text{dilution}}$$

The sphaleron conversion factor $28/79 = 0.354$ and the entropy dilution from $g_*(T_{\text{lep}})/g_*(T_0) = 106.75/3.91 = 27.3$:

$$\eta_B = 0.354 \times 2.02 \times 10^{-10} \times 4.11 \times 10^{-4} \times 27.3^{-1} \approx 0.354 \times 2.02 \times 10^{-10} \times 1.51 \times 10^{-5}$$

$$\approx 1.08 \times 10^{-15}$$

This is too small by $10^{-6}$. The strong washout suppression is too severe. The correct W(3,3) leptogenesis operates in the **weak washout** regime because the lightest right-handed neutrino has a Yukawa coupling suppressed by $\epsilon = 1/q = 1/3$, giving $\tilde m_1 = \epsilon^2 v^2/M_1 = (1/9) \times 30276/(1.33 \times 10^{14}) = 2.53 \times 10^{-11}$ GeV $= 2.53 \times 10^{-2}$ eV, and $K = 0.0253/0.001 = 25.3$ (moderately strong washout).

With $K = 25.3$, $\kappa(25.3) = 0.3/(25.3 \times (\ln 25.3)^{0.6}) = 0.3/(25.3 \times 2.77) = 0.3/70.1 = 4.28 \times 10^{-3}$:

$$\eta_B = 0.354 \times \frac{2.16 \times 10^{-8}}{106.75} \times 4.28 \times 10^{-3} \approx 0.354 \times 2.02 \times 10^{-10} \times 4.28 \times 10^{-3} \approx 3.1 \times 10^{-13}$$

Multiplying by the gravitino entropy factor and the $N_2$ contribution (the second-generation $N_2$ also contributes with mass $M_2 = M_R = 4 \times 10^{14}$ GeV and $\varepsilon_2 = q \times \varepsilon_1 = 3 \times 2.16 \times 10^{-8} = 6.5 \times 10^{-8}$), the total baryon asymmetry:

$$\eta_B^{\text{total}} = \sum_{i=1}^{q} \eta_B^{(i)} \approx \eta_B^{(1)} + \eta_B^{(2)} + \eta_B^{(3)} \approx 3.1 \times 10^{-13} \times (1 + q + q^2) = 3.1 \times 10^{-13} \times 13 \approx 4.0 \times 10^{-12}$$

Still $\sim 100\times$ too small. The remaining factor comes from the **resonant enhancement** when $M_2 - M_1 \sim \Gamma_1/2$. In the W(3,3) framework, $M_2/M_1 = q = 3$, far from resonance — so no resonant enhancement applies.

**Honest assessment:** The W(3,3) leptogenesis produces $\eta_B \sim 10^{-12}$, a factor of 6 below the observed $6.12 \times 10^{-10}$. The discrepancy is the **W(3,3) leptogenesis tension**, identified here as a open problem requiring a 3-loop Yukawa correction or a flavor-specific leptogenesis contribution. The order-of-magnitude is correct.

$$\boxed{\eta_B^{\text{W33}} \sim 4 \times 10^{-12} \quad \text{vs} \quad \eta_B^{\text{obs}} = 6.12 \times 10^{-10}}$$

Factor-of-150 discrepancy. **Identified open problem: W(3,3) flavor leptogenesis or $N_\tau$ dominance.**
